title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Issuing the Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Cases of Theft, Illegal Excavation, Illegal Trading, and Smuggling of Cultural Relics
keywords_en: theft; smuggling; illegal business operations; smuggling of cultural relics
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate

Notice on Issuing the "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Cases of Theft, Illegal Excavation, Illegal Business Operations, and Smuggling of Cultural Relics"

Fa (Yan) Fa [1987] No. 32

To the High People's Courts and People's Procuratorates of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court and Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army:

The "Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Cases of Theft, Illegal Excavation, Illegal Business Operations, and Smuggling of Cultural Relics" is hereby issued for your reference and implementation.

November 27, 1987

Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate

Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in Handling Cases of Theft, Illegal Excavation, Illegal Business Operations, and Smuggling of Cultural Relics

In recent years, criminal activities of theft, illegal excavation, illegal business operations, and smuggling of cultural relics have been rampant. Many cultural relics have been stolen and transported out of the country, or have been lost or destroyed, causing immeasurable losses to China's historical and cultural heritage. Cultural relics cannot be reproduced. Their historical, artistic, and scientific value cannot be calculated according to the "relatively large amount" or "huge amount" used for ordinary property. In order to protect historical and cultural heritage and to strike at crime severely and accurately, when handling cases of theft, illegal excavation, illegal business operations, and smuggling of cultural relics at present, the grade of the cultural relic should be taken as the standard, and the quantity of cultural relics, the assessable price, and other circumstances should be comprehensively considered. Each specific case should be analyzed concretely, and conviction and sentencing should be carried out in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law, the Law on the Protection of Cultural Relics, and the "Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Regarding the Severe Punishment of Criminals Who Seriously Undermine the Economy" (hereinafter referred to as the "Decision").

I. Theft of Cultural Relics in Museum Collections

(1) Cultural relic collections in museums, cultural relic institutions, and other cultural relic collection units all fall under cultural relics in museum collections. According to the regulations of the competent national department for cultural relics, Grade 1 and Grade 2 cultural relics in museum collections are both precious cultural relics, and Grade 3 cultural relics are generally also regarded as precious cultural relics. Cultural relics scattered in society should be graded according to the standards prescribed by the competent department for cultural relics.

(2) Whoever steals cultural relics in museum collections shall be convicted and punished as theft, applying the provisions of Articles 151 and 152 of the Criminal Law and Article 1(1) of the "Decision" of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. Whoever steals a Grade 3 cultural relic shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years, criminal detention, or public surveillance; whoever steals a Grade 2 cultural relic shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years; whoever steals a Grade 1 cultural relic shall be deemed to have committed "particularly serious circumstances" and shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years; where multiple items are stolen or a rare national treasure is stolen, a sentence of life imprisonment or the death penalty may be imposed.

(3) In a single case involving the theft of cultural relics of Grade 3 or above at various grades, the punishment may be imposed according to the sentencing range for theft of a higher-grade cultural relic; in a single case where a relatively large number of cultural relics of the same grade are stolen and the circumstances are serious, the punishment may be imposed according to the sentencing range for theft of a higher-grade cultural relic; where the circumstances are particularly serious, punishment shall be imposed according to the sentencing range for "particularly serious circumstances" provided by the Criminal Law and the "Decision" of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.

(4) Where cultural relics of Grade 3 or above in museum collections are stolen, and the competent department for cultural relics can assess their price, the assessed price may serve as a reference for sentencing.

(5) For theft of ordinary cultural relics not belonging to Grade 3 or above in museum collections, the price of the stolen items may be assessed with reference to the general retail price of the local cultural relic store in the place where the crime occurred, or the price may be assessed by the competent department for cultural relics.

(6) Theft of privately collected cultural relics may be punished with reference to the spirit of the relevant provisions above.

II. Illegal Excavation of Ancient Tombs and Ancient Cultural Sites

(1) According to the regulations of the competent national department for cultural relics, ancient tombs and ancient sites from the Qing Dynasty and earlier are protected by the State; tombs, sites, and memorial places of famous persons related to significant historical events after the Revolution of 1911 are also deemed ancient tombs and ancient sites and are protected by the State.

(2) In accordance with the provisions of Article 31 of the Law on the Protection of Cultural Relics, whoever secretly excavates an ancient tomb or ancient cultural site shall be convicted and punished as theft. When handling such cases, the determination is not limited to whether the illegally excavated ancient tomb or ancient site has already been designated as a key cultural relic protection unit; however, where an ancient tomb or ancient site that has been designated as a key cultural relic protection unit (including at the national, provincial, or county level) is illegally excavated, a heavier punishment shall be imposed.

(3) Where cultural relics are stolen or damaged during an illegal excavation, the offender shall be convicted and punished as theft, based on the grade of the stolen or damaged cultural relics, as assessed, and other circumstances.

(4) In cases of illegal excavation of ancient tombs or ancient sites that are convicted and punished as theft, the sentencing range may be determined with reference to the sentencing standards for theft of cultural relics in museum collections.

(5) Where an illegal excavation of an ancient tomb or ancient site does not result in the theft of any cultural relic, but the circumstances are serious, the offender shall also be convicted and punished as theft; if, during the illegal excavation of an ancient tomb or ancient site, precious cultural relics that are identified as immovable are damaged, a heavier punishment shall be imposed according to law.

(6) For cases of mass illegal excavation of ancient tombs or ancient sites, the principle of punishing the few and educating the majority shall be applied, with differentiated treatment. The focus of punishment shall be the ringleaders of excavation rings or mass excavations, primary offenders in joint crimes, abettors, habitual offenders, repeat offenders, and major criminals who are in collusion with offenders engaged in speculation and profiteering, smuggling, or smuggling precious cultural relics for export.

(7) Where any unit or individual loots, privately divides, or privately retains cultural relics unearthed during construction or production, the participants shall be convicted respectively as the crime of robbery or the crime of theft; if the circumstances are obviously minor, administrative penalties shall be imposed by the competent department. However, the cultural relics must be recovered and handed over to the competent department for cultural relics.

III. Destruction of Precious Cultural Relics or Scenic Spots and Historical Sites

(1) Whoever intentionally destroys precious cultural relics or scenic spots and historical sites shall, in accordance with the crime of destroying precious cultural relics or scenic spots and historical sites provided in Article 174 of the Criminal Law, be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than seven years or criminal detention.

(2) Where a criminal act of destroying precious cultural relics or scenic spots and historical sites also constitutes another crime, the offender shall be prosecuted for criminal responsibility in accordance with the heavier crime.

(3) When handling cases of destroying precious cultural relics or scenic spots and historical sites, for immovable precious cultural relics or scenic spots and historical sites (such as ancient tombs, ancient sites, ancient buildings, ancient stone carvings, revolutionary sites, revolutionary memorial buildings, scenic spots, etc.), the determination is not limited to whether they have been designated as key cultural relic protection units; if not yet designated, the competent department for cultural relics or other competent departments may assess them based on the actual circumstances.

(4) Where any unit, during capital construction or production, discovers precious cultural relics and, disregarding the advice of the competent department for cultural relics or other departments, causes damage to the precious cultural relics, if the circumstances are serious, the persons in charge and the persons directly responsible shall be investigated for criminal responsibility in accordance with Article 174 of the Criminal Law.

IV. Illegal Business Operations in Cultural Relics

(1) Illegal business operations (including purchasing, transporting, and reselling) of cultural relics, where the circumstances are serious and constitute a crime, shall be convicted and punished as the crime of speculation and profiteering, applying the provisions of Articles 117 and 118 of the Criminal Law and Article 1(1) of the "Decision" of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. Where Grade 3 cultural relics are illegally dealt in, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention, and may concurrently or solely be fined or have property confiscated; where Grade 2 cultural relics are illegally dealt in, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years, and may concurrently be sentenced to confiscation of property; where Grade 1 cultural relics are illegally dealt in, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, and may concurrently be sentenced to confiscation of property; where multiple items are illegally dealt in or a rare national treasure is illegally dealt in, this constitutes "particularly serious circumstances," and a sentence of life imprisonment or the death penalty may be imposed, concurrently with confiscation of property. For a single case involving illegal dealing in cultural relics of Grade 3 or above at various grades, or illegal dealing in multiple items of the same grade, the relevant provisions of Article 1(3) of this Interpretation may be referred to for sentencing.

(2) Where Grade 3 or above cultural relics are illegally dealt in, and the competent department for cultural relics can assess their price, the assessed price and the illegal proceeds of the criminal may serve as a reference for sentencing.

(3) Where a unit illegally deals in Grade 3 or above cultural relics, the persons in charge and the persons directly responsible may be investigated for criminal responsibility with reference to the above provisions.

(4) Where an individual illegally deals in ordinary cultural relics not belonging to Grade 3 or above, if the illegal turnover is 5,000 yuan or more, or the illegal gains are 1,000 yuan or more, the offender shall be prosecuted for criminal responsibility as the crime of speculation and profiteering.

Where a unit illegally deals in ordinary cultural relics, if the illegal turnover is 100,000 yuan or more, or the illegal gains are 50,000 yuan or more, the persons in charge and the persons directly responsible shall be prosecuted for criminal responsibility as the crime of speculation and profiteering; if the illegal turnover is less than 100,000 yuan, or the illegal gains are less than 50,000 yuan, but the circumstances are serious, the persons in charge and the persons directly responsible shall also be prosecuted for criminal responsibility as the crime of speculation and profiteering.

V. Smuggling of Cultural Relics

(1) Smuggling precious cultural relics (including Grade 1, 2, and 3) out of the country shall be convicted and punished as the crime of smuggling precious cultural relics for export, applying Article 173 of the Criminal Law; smuggling ordinary cultural relics not belonging to precious cultural relics out of the country shall be convicted and punished as the crime of smuggling, applying Articles 116 and 118 of the Criminal Law. Where the circumstances of either crime are particularly serious, Article 1(1) of the "Decision" of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall apply.

(2) Any of the following acts constitutes the crime of smuggling precious cultural relics for export:

1. Evading customs supervision, transporting, carrying, or sending precious cultural relics out of the country by post;
2. Purchasing precious cultural relics for the purpose of smuggling them for export;
3. Knowing that another person is smuggling precious cultural relics for export, selling precious cultural relics to that person, or introducing that person to purchase precious cultural relics, or transporting, carrying, or sending precious cultural relics for that person, or providing a transit place for that person;
4. Privately selling precious cultural relics to foreigners or residents outside the country (including Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan).

(3) Sentencing for the crime of smuggling precious cultural relics for export: Where Grade 3 precious cultural relics are smuggled for export, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than five years, and may concurrently be fined; where Grade 2 precious cultural relics are smuggled for export, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years, and may concurrently be fined; where Grade 1 precious cultural relics are smuggled for export, this constitutes "particularly serious circumstances," and the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, and may concurrently be sentenced to confiscation of property; where multiple items are smuggled for export or a rare national treasure is smuggled for export, a sentence of life imprisonment or the death penalty may be imposed, concurrently with confiscation of property. For a single case involving the smuggling of precious cultural relics of various grades for export, or the smuggling of multiple items of the same grade for export, the relevant provisions of Article 1(3) of this Interpretation may be referred to for sentencing.

(4) Where precious cultural relics are smuggled for export, and the competent department for cultural relics can assess the price of the precious cultural relics, the assessed price and the illegal gains of the criminal may serve as a reference for sentencing.

(5) Where a unit smuggles precious cultural relics for export, the persons in charge and the persons directly responsible may be investigated for criminal responsibility with reference to the relevant provisions.

(6) Where an individual smuggles ordinary cultural relics not belonging to precious cultural relics, if the smuggling amount is 5,000 yuan or more, or the illegal gains are 1,000 yuan or more, the offender shall be prosecuted for criminal responsibility as the crime of smuggling.

Where a unit smuggles ordinary cultural relics, if the smuggling amount is 100,000 yuan or more, or the illegal gains are 50,000 yuan or more, the persons in charge and the persons directly responsible shall be prosecuted for criminal responsibility as the crime of smuggling, and the unit shall be sentenced to a fine and confiscation of the smuggled cultural relics, smuggling transport tools, and illegal gains; if the smuggling amount is less than 100,000 yuan, or the illegal gains are less than 50,000 yuan, but the circumstances are serious, the persons in charge and the persons directly responsible shall also be prosecuted for criminal responsibility as the crime of smuggling, and the unit shall be sentenced to a fine and confiscation of the smuggled cultural relics, smuggling transport tools, and illegal gains.

(7) Whoever colludes with criminals outside the country (including Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan) to smuggle precious cultural relics for export or to smuggle ordinary cultural relics shall be given a heavier punishment according to law.

VI. Punishment of Crimes Committed by State Functionaries

(1) If a State functionary, by taking advantage of his office or by collusion with persons inside or outside the unit, commits any of the crimes listed in the above articles of this Interpretation, or commits the crime of embezzlement or acceptance of bribes involving cultural relics, he shall be given a heavier punishment according to law.

(2) If a State functionary neglects his duty, resulting in the theft, destruction, or loss of cultural relics, causing significant losses, he shall be convicted and punished as the crime of neglect of duty.

VII. Appraisal of Cultural Relics

(1) When handling the above types of cases, if appraisal of cultural relics is necessary, the competent department for cultural relics of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government, or the competent department for cultural relics of a region or a municipality under provincial jurisdiction that it designates as having the conditions for appraisal, shall organize persons with specialized knowledge to participate; where assessment of the price of cultural relics is required, the same procedure shall be followed.

When conducting the above appraisal of cultural relics or assessment of cultural relic prices, at least three appraisers designated by the competent department for cultural relics and engaged by the judicial organs must participate. The appraisers shall produce a written appraisal or assessment.

(2) If a dispute arises during the handling of a case concerning the appraisal of cultural relics or the assessment of their prices, the matter shall be submitted to the competent department for cultural relics of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government for review by specially assigned persons. If a dispute still arises, the matter shall be submitted to the competent national department for cultural relics for review by specially assigned persons.

(3) For cases where the defendant is sentenced to death, the written appraisal of cultural relics shall be reviewed by specially assigned persons organized by the competent national department for cultural relics.

Appendix:

Relevant Provisions of the "Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Cultural Relics"

Article 31: Anyone who commits any of the following acts shall be investigated for criminal responsibility according to law:

(1) Embezzling or stealing State-owned cultural relics;
(2) Smuggling precious cultural relics for export or engaging in speculation and profiteering in cultural relics where the circumstances are serious;
(3) Intentionally destroying precious cultural relics protected by the State or scenic spots and historical sites;
(4) Where a State functionary neglects his duty, causing damage or loss of precious cultural relics, if the circumstances are serious.

Whoever secretly excavates ancient cultural sites or ancient tombs shall be convicted as theft.

Whoever privately sells a privately collected precious cultural relic to a foreigner shall be convicted as smuggling precious cultural relics for export.

Where a cultural relic worker steals from his own custody the cultural relics under his management, he shall be given a heavier punishment according to law.

Relevant Provisions of the "Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China"

Article 151: Whoever steals, swindles, or forcibly seizes a relatively large amount of public or private property shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years, criminal detention, or public surveillance.

Article 152: A habitual thief, a habitual swindler, or one who steals, swindles, or forcibly seizes a huge amount of public or private property shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years but not more than ten years; if the circumstances are particularly serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years or life imprisonment, and may concurrently be sentenced to confiscation of property.

Article 174: Whoever intentionally destroys precious cultural relics or scenic spots and historical sites protected by the State shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than seven years or criminal detention.

Article 117: Whoever violates financial, foreign exchange, precious metals, or industrial and commercial management regulations by engaging in speculation and profiteering, if the circumstances are serious, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention, and may concurrently or solely be fined or have property confiscated.

Article 116: Whoever violates customs regulations by engaging in smuggling, if the circumstances are serious, shall, in addition to having the smuggled articles confiscated and may be fined in accordance with customs regulations, be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than three years or criminal detention, and may concurrently be sentenced to confiscation of property.

Article 118: Whoever habitually engages in smuggling or speculation and profiteering, smuggles or speculates in a huge amount, or is a ringleader of a smuggling or speculation ring shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years, and may concurrently be sentenced to confiscation of property.

Article 173: Whoever violates the regulations on the protection of cultural relics by smuggling precious cultural relics for export shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years, and may concurrently be fined; if the circumstances are serious, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years or life imprisonment, and may concurrently be sentenced to confiscation of property.

Relevant Provisions of the "Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress Regarding the Severe Punishment of Criminals Who Seriously Undermine the Economy"

I. The following supplements and amendments are made to the relevant provisions of the Criminal Law:

(1) The penalties for the crime of smuggling, exchange speculation, and speculation and profiteering for exorbitant profits under Article 118 of the Criminal Law, the crime of theft under Article 152, the crime of drug trafficking under Article 171, and the crime of smuggling precious cultural relics for export under Article 173 are respectively supplemented or amended as follows: where the circumstances are particularly serious, the offender shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, life imprisonment, or death, and may concurrently be sentenced to confiscation of property.

Relevant Provisions of the "Customs Law of the People's Republic of China"

Article 47(3): Where a person commits the crime of smuggling, the People's Court shall impose a criminal penalty according to law, including a fine, and confiscation of the smuggled goods, articles, smuggling transport tools, and illegal gains.

Article 47(4): Where an enterprise, institution, State organ, or social organization commits the crime of smuggling, the judicial organs shall investigate the criminal responsibility of its persons in charge and the persons directly responsible according to law; and the unit shall be sentenced to a fine and confiscation of the smuggled goods, articles, smuggling transport tools, and illegal gains.
